cases.description: The refactor names two real targets: `cache.py` (the rename source, resolved to engine/cache.py) and `cache_layer.py` (the rename destination, which does not yet exist in the report). This is expected for a rename -- the new name legitimately has nothing to resolve to before the rename happens, unlike a genuinely mistyped or fabricated target.
cases.grounding: engine/target_resolver.py resolved `cache.py` to engine/cache.py by module-stem match; `cache_layer.py` correctly returned resolved_module_path=None since no such module exists yet.

cases.description: engine/cache.py has real structural risk (fan_in=1, boundary-changing rename operation -> medium tier) but it is genuinely covered: tests/test_cache.py imports engine.cache directly, so this is a verified-risk situation, not a silent one.
cases.grounding: target_resolver.py found engine/session.py as a caller (fan_in=1); test_coverage_scanner.py found tests/test_cache.py importing engine.cache, so no untested-blast-radius flag fired.
